findings: apprunner.yaml Python version mismatch — runtime: python311 and runtime-version: "3.11" conflict with the project's Python 3.12 stack (Dockerfile uses python:3.12-slim). Change both to python312 / "3.12", or remove the file if App Runner is expected to run the Docker image rather than a managed runtime.

apprunner.yaml port mismatch — run.command binds to port 8080, but the Docker image exposes 8000 and deploy-backend.sh documents 8000. App Runner will route traffic to 8080 but the container listens on 8000 — the service will not respond. Change the port in apprunner.yaml to 8000 (or align the Dockerfile and deploy script to 8080 if that was intentional).

Ignored upload return value in simulate() and _ingest_device() — Both callers discard the bool returned by _upload_clip_to_s3, then unconditionally record clip_file as if upload succeeded. On failure the local file is not deleted (correct) but clip_file is stored in the DB pointing to a key that S3 doesn't have. The clip route will generate a valid-looking pre-signed URL that resolves to a 403/404 from S3. Fix: check the return value and set clip_file = None (or a sentinel) when the upload fails.
